metric: Total network vehicle-hours-lost (VHL) — relative reduction, impact-priority vs nearest-first
balancedNote: When the fleet is large enough that the queue drains (N=25, balanced regime) the kernel gain collapses to ~8% — priority dispatch only buys VHL while the fleet cannot keep up.
honestCaveat: CITE THE DECOUPLED (SUMO-grounded) RESULT. The +53% kernel headline used a CIRCULAR cost — the per-incident cost was the impact score's own kernel (Spearman 0.93 with the score), so it largely measured 'acting on the score reduces the cost the score predicts'. With an INDEPENDENT SUMO-physics cost (Spearman 0.51 with the score) priority dispatch is 38% WORSE than nearest-first (N=15), negative at every fleet size, in all 90 seeds. H2 is NOT SUPPORTED under the honest cost. VHL is a relative index, not calibrated absolute hours — only the ratio between policies is interpreted.
